target_customer: Professionals and teams wanting instant browser video meetings without sign-up
problem: Video meetings required installed software or accounts. Meetings.io gave a reusable room link where anyone could drop in from a browser.
business_model: Free consumer and prosumer product with no revenue model stated at launch

founders.name: Denis Mars
founders.background_notes: YC profile describes him as a repeat founder with exits; details not opened. Dealroom (single source, not opened in full) says he later became Director of Admissions at YC.

founders.name: Arend Naylor
founders.background_notes: YC profile lists CTO roles at Koan and Embedster plus Bitplay; dates not given so not recorded as prior employers. YC profile also shows batch W2011, conflicting with the W2010 listing.

competitors.name: Skype
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch at the April 2012 launch

technical_complexity.rationale: Browser video and chat with screen sharing and no plugins was hard in 2010 to 2012 before WebRTC matured, though a team of two to three built it.

defensibility.rationale: Free product with no lock-in; WebRTC made browser video available to any competitor and big incumbents already offered similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google Hangouts and Skype already covered the use case. Jive bought the team and product in November 2012 and later turned the features into Jive Chime.

market_need_then: Skype and Hangouts required software or accounts; TechCrunch framed the no-install room link as the pain solved. First eight hours of launch reportedly drew 13,000 to 15,000 users per one search summary, not verified in an opened source.

branding.domain_note: Product used the meetings.io domain; the company was Bitplay Inc. Domain acquisition history not found. meetings.io now redirects to bloomgrowth.com.

brand_strength.rationale: Product name was descriptive and generic with a .io domain. Limited press about the brand itself; the coverage focused on the WebRTC technology and acquisition.

outcome_analysis: Bitplay built Meetings.io, a browser video meeting room product, and launched publicly in April 2012 with a seed round of just under one million dollars from Yuri Milner and SV Angel. Jive Software acquired it in November 2012, and Jive shipped the features during 2013 as Jive Chime. The exit came from timing at the start of WebRTC and a small team with working browser video rather than from traction or a durable moat.
notes: YC one-liner says acquired by Jive in 2013 but press release and TechCrunch date the deal to 5 November 2012; the 2013 date is the integration year. Combined deal value with Producteev reported in one search summary as 7.6 million dollars plus stock, not separable, so exit amount is null. Aggregator totals for funding (1.8M, 1.36M) conflict and are unverified. Seed round date is the TechCrunch report date; the closing date is not stated.
